adrCandidates.title: PLC content exchange via Siemens external source (UDT, DB, SCL) with strict single-object writes
adrCandidates.context: Block XML is the only round-trip format at first; users need readable source for UDTs, global DBs and SCL FB/FC/OB. Openness external-source import (GenerateBlocksFromSource) has no multiplicity switch, creates every object a file declares (including unknown types), and CreateFromFile leaves a PlcExternalSource node behind. The test project cannot reference Siemens types.
adrCandidates.decision: format=source is added in phases (UDT, then global DB, then SCL) behind a language-aware eligibility gate; type ops default to source, block ops default to xml. Writes are strict updates declaring exactly one object that matches the target (checked by a comment/string-aware declaration scanner), never upserts; reads choose multiplicity via withDependencies (default false, closure is context-only, no hash). GenerateOptions are passed explicitly everywhere. The temporary external-source node is removed by a scope and a leftover is a postcondition failure. BOM/CRLF are normalised on export/import. update_block_logic returns a closed typed blockImportOutcome (conservative tri-state mutation boundary, NotSent/Sent/Unknown dispatch assigned at control-flow seams, bounded and sanitised, capability-gated against stale workers). Logic is split into unit-tested Siemens-free halves and thin Siemens shells. STL and non-SCL languages stay on xml. Live spike findings (instance DBs survive interface change, header attributes preserved, 2-arg export default is None, unit-scoped resolution) and two traps (stale handle after block recreation, auto-rename of colliding members to <name>_1) are recorded as consequences.
adrCandidates.consequences: Callers get readable round-trippable source for UDT/DB/SCL with one object per write; multi-object source is refused. STL/LAD/FBD/GRAPH remain XML-only. Import truthfulness is explicit but ContentRelation stays unknown. Offset-column handling was dropped after live evidence showed no such column. The Siemens-free/shell split limits unit-test reach of the shell code, so live gates carry the burden (harness scripts since removed). docs/SupportedOperations/IMPORT_EXPORT_OPTIONS_SUMMARY.md is stale (still says FB/FC/OB are not source-eligible) and should be fixed alongside the ADR.
adrCandidates.overlapWithExistingDocs: docs/SupportedOperations/IMPORT_EXPORT_OPTIONS_SUMMARY.md already holds the format/default table, GenerateBlockOption.None, temporarySourceState and the blockImportOutcome vocabulary (12,000-char cap); PLC_OPERATIONS_SUMMARY.md has the format/withDependencies rows and 'source declaring more than one object is refused'; docs/roadmap/export-import-format.md carries phase status. The ADR should hold only the why (strict update, single-object, explicit options, spike findings and traps) and point to those pages; no matching IMPROVEMENT_LOG entry beyond OB/large-block follow-ups.

adrCandidates.title: plc_read / plc_write on the guarded single-call pipeline replace token-bound snapshot batches
adrCandidates.context: The first PLC write path was a generic batch with safety tokens bound to typed snapshots (update_tag exact-target snapshot with OperationCapability.SafetyRead in PR3, then per-operation tag/table/constant scopes with whole-PLC namespace collision probes in PR5). It was live-accepted but heavy, coupled preview to apply, included start_plc/stop_plc, and diverged from the Network model. Earlier read-side defects (compile identity, cross-reference completeness) and missing block header metadata were fixed along the way.
adrCandidates.decision: Retire tokens, SafetyRead, snapshot readers, the legacy write audit and start_plc/stop_plc; replace the three generic batch tools with plc_read, read_cross_references and plc_write on the structured contract and the shared guarded pipeline (ConfirmsEveryCall=false, only block/info guards, zero elicitation, audit v2). Planning uses public typed reads only. Content writes use expectedContentHash in the write's own format, checked at plan time and again as a worker precondition (state_changed; over-budget content cannot be written); PlcSoftwareLocator.FindUnique makes ambiguous plcName fail the call; dependsOn lets later items rely on earlier creates. Read integrity rules: plcName is PlcSoftware.Name and deviceName the container, Siemens compile totals are never recomputed and diagnostics are budget-projected; cross-reference owners ship only when verified live, partial coverage is IsComplete=false; block header Author/Version/Family/Name are read via typed properties only (never GetAttribute, which can throw over remoting and stall for minutes), default-on additive details, no flag or version bump, reported metadata not provenance.
adrCandidates.consequences: One write model across Network/PLC/HMI/VCI; tokens and snapshot readers must not be reintroduced. Unverified cross-reference owner kinds stay unshipped. Header reads were never live-accepted. Several plc_write parts (collision/exists guards, dependsOn replanning, presence re-reads) were later removed by the native-rejections ADR; tool counts moved 6/15/15 then to today's 8/19/19.
adrCandidates.overlapWithExistingDocs: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md section 8 'PLC writes (plc_write)' and 'Guarded write pipeline' already describe the current pipeline, guards and audit; AGENTS.md 'Write safety model' states tokens/SafetyRead are retired; PLC_OPERATIONS_SUMMARY.md has read/write tables, cross-reference coverage and 'Unverified owner kinds' (which links Appendix B of the 2026-10-05 spec); PROJECT_OPERATIONS_SUMMARY.md and ARCHITECTURE project-tree section cover header details. IMPROVEMENT_LOG 'Open: plc_write follow-ups (PR B)' and 'PLC read and cross-reference follow-ups (PR A)' hold open items. The ADR should record only the token-to-pipeline pivot and its rationale (and the typed-property-only header rule), and cross-reference the write-safety-redesign ADR from another cluster.

adrCandidates.title: TIA Portal is the authority on its own rejections; plc_write stops re-implementing them
adrCandidates.context: After plc_write shipped, hosts and workers duplicated Portal checks (name collisions, existing targets, default tag table), costing planning reads and time, while the real native error was hidden. Live testing showed Portal does reject these cases, but also silently ignores a colliding update_tag rename, and that a duplicate singleton OB never reached Portal through the tool.
adrCandidates.decision: Remove duplicate collision/exists/default-table guards and worker preconditions, in-call replanning and presence re-reads; keep what Openness cannot supply: delete-consequence and address-overlap guards, optimistic content-hash concurrency, content-hash re-export verification, and plc_ob_singleton_exists. Add the closed category engineering_rejected for an EngineeringTargetInvocationException thrown inside a mutation worker method (other EngineeringException stays worker_operation_failed; portal_lost wins), classified by exception type only never message text, with a bounded conditional engineeringError {type,message,inner[]}. update_tag applies rename first and reads Name back, failing postcondition_failed. plc_write contract bumps to 2.0 (plc_read stays 1.0). Timing is compared only on the same project copy and warm worker, and Network, then HMI, then VCI follow with their own baselines.
adrCandidates.consequences: Less planning work and verbatim Portal diagnostics, at the price that collision directions beyond the live-tested ones are unverified and engineering_rejected does not prove a setter was reached. PLC content importers and VCI still flatten Siemens failures without engineeringError. The same principle was later applied to Network and HMI (cross-cluster; merge with those ADRs if the maintainer wants one principle ADR).
adrCandidates.overlapWithExistingDocs: AGENTS.md 'Failure categories from Siemens' and ARCHITECTURE.md section 8 (PLC writes, first paragraph states the authority principle and the kept guards) plus PLC_OPERATIONS_SUMMARY.md 'Failures from TIA Portal' and 'Tag safety acceptance boundary' already carry the rules; IMPROVEMENT_LOG 'Completed: plc_write native rejections (2026-10-26)' and 'Open: plc_write native rejections follow-ups' carry outcomes/timings/open items. The ADR should add only the rationale and the 'keep vs. delegate to Portal' test, pointing to those.

adrCandidates.title: Bounded, cursor-based read contracts for large project reads
adrCandidates.context: Hardware and project-tree reads overran the 60k-char value budget on large projects (issues #31, #32). The first step split get_project_status/browse_project_tree/compile_check out of execute_read_batch, then enumeration completeness, opt-in hardware pagination and the v3 tree were added.
adrCandidates.decision: Move project reads to standalone tools with a per-result budget and no aliases. One worker-local ProjectDeviceEnumerator feeds hardware and tree. Hardware pages use a split worker/host seam (worker descriptors, host canonical sizing). Tree v3 is a single breaking contract: typed startSelector and host-owned immutable in-memory snapshots, so continuations make zero worker calls. Cursors are HMAC-protected, process-local and binding-pinned. Pages are whole entities or omissions, never truncated. Direct Openness pruning is gated on measurement.
adrCandidates.consequences: Cursors do not survive host restart (snapshot_unavailable). Reads give a stable-set view, not a transaction. The sealed vocabulary is cursor_binding_mismatch, invalid_selector, snapshot_* and result_*_too_large. Rejected: dual legacy/modern modes, worker or disk snapshots, truncation, overlapping subtrees. The resolver-optimization follow-up stays open.
adrCandidates.overlapWithExistingDocs: ARCHITECTURE.md section 3 'Project enumeration completeness' and 'Project-tree v3 snapshot and continuation seam' plus section 7a 'Hardware configuration pagination seam' carry the mechanics and limits; PROJECT_OPERATIONS_SUMMARY.md 'browse_project_tree v3' carries the contract and failure vocabulary; IMPROVEMENT_LOG 'Open: Deeper project-tree resolver optimization' carries the follow-up. The ADR should hold only why (split seam, snapshot vs transaction, rejected options) and link to those sections.

adrCandidates.title: Network as an independent domain on a shared canonical-JSON kernel with exact fail-closed identity
adrCandidates.context: Network ops began inside the generic batch tools with escaped-string results. Phases 1-3 split them out, made results single-layer structured JSON and added identity/introspection reads; live runs then showed node IDs are only unique per owning interface and that optional metadata must not veto writes.
adrCandidates.decision: Hard-cut network ops out of generic batches (no aliases) into network_read/network_write with their own request/catalog/invoker over a domain-neutral OperationBatches kernel. adrCandidates.title: Network writes: subnet lifecycle, guarded single-call pipeline and trusting native Portal rejections
adrCandidates.context: Network writes started as token-gated preview/apply with server-side re-implementation of Portal rules, then gained subnet create/update/delete (Phase 4). Safety tokens, elicitation, post-write read-back and per-check rules proved heavy and diverged from what Portal itself reports.
adrCandidates.decision: Subnet lifecycle is three explicit operations with exact subnetId selectors, one ExclusiveAccess transaction each, minimal result, connected delete allowed with an unchanged-root-device-count postcondition (one mutate op and a separate tool rejected). Writes moved to the guarded single-call pipeline: dryRun replaces confirm/token, no elicitation, only info (connected delete) and block (unreadable inventory) guards, unknown evidence never equals empty. Contract 2.0 trusts Portal as authoritative: non-throwing call counts as landed, throwing is typed engineering_rejected/worker_operation_failed with verbatim engineeringError, configure stops at first rejection with a conditional applied-subset outcome, portal_lost wins, and a shared TrustedWriteVerifier with per-domain policies marks items trusted/superseded without read-back. Typed Node/IoConnector calls replaced reflection; the colliding subnet rename is the single retained postcondition check.
adrCandidates.consequences: Cheap planning (one hardware snapshot) but partial application is possible with no rollback, so callers re-read with network_read before retry; duplicate IP/PN-name collisions surface only in compile; failed items carry no verification entry; same-call connect-then-delete under-lists nodes. PLC and HMI reuse the verifier. Undo remains a separate unstarted investigation.

adrCandidates.title: Retire preview/apply safety tokens in favour of a guarded single-call write pipeline
adrCandidates.context: The first write-safety design used preview_write_batch plus an apply token over a state hash (hardened across PRs 1-6: preview diffs, narrowed snapshot scopes, SafetyRead). Client spike (2026-09-29) showed elicitation works but the anthropic/requiresUserInteraction marker is honoured only by Claude Code. The V21 OnlineProvider probe also showed no public Start/Stop or RUN/STOP read, so PLC run/stop was deferred and later removed.
adrCandidates.decision: Replace tokens with one call: validate, verified binding, pinned lease, plan, guards, dryRun stop, mutate, verify, audit. Use a dryRun flag instead of a preview tool; mandatory format-tagged expectedContentHash (If-Match style) on content replacement only; elicitation as the user-asking mechanism with every non-accept outcome denying and no claim of proved human consent; drop the approval marker; one canonical audit record behind a sink. Generic batch tools, token core, SafetyRead and the legacy audit stream were deleted; new write domains must build on Safety/Pipeline and must not reintroduce tokens. Per-item failure categories now come from the shared item projection, not the old batch field.

adrCandidates.title: Capability-class access modes, fail-closed identity policy and advisory tool annotations
adrCandidates.context: Write access began as mode names gating tools. Review of PR #29 found missing-identity handling inconsistent between real worker, FakeWorker and fixtures, and same-path forceRebind kept stale verified identity. The redesign added a third full tier and a confirm switch, later superseded when lifecycle moved into read-write and OnlineControl was removed. MCP annotations were added as client hints.
adrCandidates.decision: Access tiers are capability-class presets, with the ceiling enforced at discovery, host dispatch and worker dispatch, never per-tool allow lists; unknown operations and invalid modes are denied in every mode; one shared mode-name helper and one shared tool registration used by tests. OperationPolicyCatalog.RequiresExpectedSessionIdentity is the single fail-closed authority (Observe, TemporaryExport, open/create may omit identity; a supplied identity is always validated), shared by worker and FakeWorker, separate from access authorization. adrCandidates.title: Lifecycle confirmation follows access mode; explicit binding; content tools act on the bound project only

adrCandidates.title: Multiuser support through a typed ProjectBase root with lifecycle owners, discovery on bind_project
adrCandidates.context: TIA V21 Multiuser local sessions need first-class support without a second process, a repo-owned facade or a new read tool. adrCandidates.decision: Use the Siemens-typed common root (ProjectBase) plus a lifecycle owner (StandaloneProjectOwner or LocalSessionOwner) in a single internal ActiveProjectContext. All discovery and inspection stays on bind_project actions, with no new tool and the same tool counts. Local-session identity is the typed .amc21 engineering path with exact PID/owner/generation continuity, and .als21 is only opener input recorded as nullable provenance. Mode, remote identity and active connection stay unknown or null unless a supported join proves them. Connection state is observation-only and never asserted. Wire identity stays a projection of session state, not a stored copy.
adrCandidates.consequences: Standalone behavior is preserved and there is one binding model for both container kinds. Cold adoption has null ALS provenance, and same-path or ambiguous owners fail closed (the separate-session-ID follow-up remains open in the improvement log). Mode and remote association are unavailable until Siemens exposes a join. Reflection is a documented last resort only. Discovery stays bounded by the existing 60,000/180,000 budgets.

adrCandidates.title: hmi_write: typed guarded writes that leave Portal's rules to Portal
adrCandidates.context: hmi_write 1.0 copied the plc_write pipeline with a full planner, collision/existence guards, a locate cache and read-back verification. Live probes showed Portal itself rejects or reports most of these cases, so the host duplicated rules and the verifier cost far more code than it was worth.
adrCandidates.decision: Use typed operations (tag tables, bound tags, discrete/analog alarms) on the guarded single-call pipeline rather than a property bag, with fixed setter order and identity-checked cleanup of failed creates. Eventtext is plain text wrapped by the server, and there is no connection creation. The 2.0 refactor adopts the guard rule that the server guards only writes Portal neither rejects (O1) nor reports afterwards (O2). Collision, existence, and bound-tag dataType refusals are retired, planning is target-only, and guards reduce to three (hmi_state_unverifiable plus two delete info guards). Verification moves to the shared TrustedWriteVerifier with no read-back, and the HMI-side check is hmi_read validate plus the Portal UI compile. Typed engineering_rejected carries engineeringError, and portal_lost wins on every write path. 'Connection requires plcTag' is kept because connection-only assignment was never probed.
adrCandidates.consequences: Much less host code (HmiWriteVerifier removed) and Portal remains the authority. Callers must inspect state, Validate and compile separately. Duplicate Create semantics, case-only rename and connection-only assignment remain unprobed limits. Supersession keys are flat per object, and outcome-bearing refusals can supersede earlier success (R1). Qualification is scoped to R1/R2/R3, with no full .113 rerun.

adrCandidates.title: VCI as standalone-only workspace primitives with leaf-expanded scopes and breadcrumb-based loss recovery
adrCandidates.context: VCI (Version Control Interface) workspaces and mappings needed MCP exposure. Open choices were: reads inside an existing tool vs a new tool, whether the server should drive Git/connect/workspace upkeep, whether to cap scopes or let the worker expand them, how Openness behaves on containers (risky) and how to report progress when a long import or export kills Portal. Live findings on 2026-10-16 (HMI mapping paths, export scan cost, same-session recovery after Portal restart) then refined the first design.
adrCandidates.decision: Add a separate vci_read (all modes) because status costs about 0.5 s per mapping and the gate differs, and vci_write (read-write/full). Tools are primitives: Git, workspace upkeep, connect, workspace groups, VCI settings and library scopes stay with the user or out of scope. Standalone .ap21 only. Scopes are uncapped, but the worker expands to leaves and Openness never receives a container; results are counts plus lastAttempted. Imports run per item inside one ExclusiveAccess transaction after a status prefilter; other writes run plain; sync touches only source-changed leaves and skips conflicts. Unknown status is passed raw and treated as a conflict. A per-leaf breadcrumb file lets the host name the last attempted leaf after a kill, and portal_lost invalidates binding immediately. HMI mapping paths are repaired by project/device/software ownership proof, never guessed names or cached native handles. Export collision checks are not replaced by snapshots or caches; the leaves x mappings scan growth is recorded rather than claimed fixed. Recovery after Portal loss reopens only after fresh empty-attachment proof and explicit open_project forceRebind. VCI keeps its own scope vocabulary (adds TechnologyObject, HmiSoftware, ScriptModule), keys mappings relative to the workspace root and keeps a private path policy for now. Breadcrumb ids travel inside VciWriteRequestInfo so WorkerRequest and protocol version are unchanged.
adrCandidates.consequences: The surface is small, safe by construction (no container ever reaches Openness) and recoverable after Portal loss, but long exports are slow and unbounded, local sessions, software units, system blocks and library scopes remain unsupported, and VCI does not use the shared verifier or typed engineeringError. The path-policy duplication and export scan growth stay open in the improvement log. Live acceptance recorded a failed frozen candidate and a scoped pass for the repaired candidate; wider native coverage is untested.

The ADR should hold only the why (primitives principle, separate tool, leaf-only, rejected scopes, no cache/snapshot) and link to these rather than restate mechanics.

toolDescriptions: client.py: a stdin-driven JSON-RPC stdio client for the installed global tool (~/.dotnet/tools/tia-mcp.exe). It is not self-scheduling.

client.py inputs: env HMI_TIMING_PROJECT (an absolute .ap21 path) and HMI_TIMING_PROJECT_SHA256, which it checks against the file. One JSON command per stdin line: {name,args,label}, {restore:true,label} or {stop:true}.

client.py behaviour: it verifies `dotnet tool list --global` shows exactly EXPECTED_VERSION. It launches the server with `--access-mode full --max-item-chars 1000000 --max-document-chars 1000000 --worker-timeout-minutes 15`, sends initialize with protocol 2025-06-18, and asserts serverInfo == {TiaMcpServer, 4.2.0.0}.
client.py request handling: a reader thread plus a queue enforces a 900 s deadline per request. A timeout writes pending-call.json and stops, with no replay or cleanup.

client.py per-call work: it writes <label>-request.json and <label>.json (refusing to overwrite). It asserts the text block equals structuredContent and appends to measurements.jsonl. For hmi_write it finds the matching audit v2 record in %LOCALAPPDATA%\TiaMcpServer\audit\writes-*.jsonl by identical responseText, appends to audits.jsonl, and computes rootMs / itemSumMs / remainderMs.

client.py hard-coded HMI specifics: the tool name 'hmi_write', the contractVersion assertion, the EXPECTED_VERSION pin, and the validate_write phase/count checks. restore() runs close_project(saveBeforeClose:false), open_project, re-hashes the project and asserts get_project_status isOpen=true, isModified=false.

client.py writes outputs next to the script (ROOT = script dir): server-stderr.log, initialize.json, provenance.json, measurements.jsonl, audits.jsonl and the per-call files. That is why each PR copied the whole folder.

The scheduling order (restore, an untimed full hmi_read, then the workload, for runs 0-3 over H1..H5) exists nowhere as code. It is described only in the baseline README, and an external driver, not archived, fed stdin. The after report mentions a 'timing driver' and a driver-provenance.json that is not in the repo (hash only in the manifest rawInputs). A shared script must include this scheduler.

It also checks 22 complete reads (101 tags, 9 tables, 4 alarms, canonical hash) and 66 redacted lifecycle projections.

findings: Use linguist-generated only. Linguist's overrides.md summary table says: linguist-generated = 'Excluded from stats, hidden in diffs'; linguist-vendored and linguist-documentation = 'Excluded from stats' only, and the text says 'unlike vendored and documentation files, these files are suppressed in diffs'. Linguist issue #2206 (maintainer arfon, 2015; closed/locked by lildude 2017) confirms vendored does NOT hide PR diffs on github.com, only generated does. linguist-detectable only affects language stats (data/prose types). So documentation/vendored/detectable are useless for this goal.

GitHub's official page ('Customizing how changed files appear on GitHub') says linguist-generated marks paths 'ignored for the repository's language statistics and hidden by default in diffs', uses the same matching rules as .gitignore, and gives the example 'search/index.json linguist-generated'. It does not mention 'collapsed', 'Load diff', pull requests, file types or renamed/deleted files. Collapse-by-default and click-to-load come from secondary sources (thoughtbot 2017/2019) and the banner 'Some generated files are not rendered by default' seen on real PR pages; the exact current UI label is unverified here.

Path/glob semantics verified locally with git 2.55 check-attr in a scratch repo outside the project: '/docs/superpowers/specs/**' and '/docs/superpowers/acceptance/reports/inputs/**' match all depths, any extension (md, json, gz, png, even nested .gitattributes files). A bare directory pattern ('/dir/' with trailing slash, or '/dir' alone) matches NOTHING for files inside, so '/**' is required. A later '-linguist-generated' line re-expands a single kept file (last match wins). The attribute lookup is purely path-based and file existence on disk is irrelevant (a nonexistent path still reports 'set').

Linguist docs state paths in .gitattributes are relative to the file's location and examples include 'dir/*' and 'ano-dir/**'; the docs say nothing about file type restrictions. generated.rb's built-in heuristics are type-specific, but the explicit attribute is an unconditional override, so Markdown/JSON/gz/png are expected to work. Direct evidence that a .md file collapses on a PR is not found in docs; treat as needing the test PR.

Stats: the Linguist effect on language stats is documented, but this repo's language bar is only C# and PowerShell (gh api languages), and Markdown/JSON are not counted by default, so the stats effect here is nil. Whether collapsed files still count in the PR '+N -M' summary and 'N files changed' is NOT documented; one report (paritytech/substrate#13628) says diff stats still included the generated file. Assume they still count (the file list and totals stay, only the diff body is hidden) and confirm on the test PR.

Reviewability: collapsed files remain in the file list and diff can be loaded on demand ('click through to have it loaded' per thoughtbot; banner text on PR pages 'Some generated files are not rendered by default'). Collapsing also applies to commit and compare views. Effect on the PR file tree, code search and rendering of deleted or renamed files is undocumented and unverified; GitHub docs mention nothing, so these must be checked in the UI. Per-file 'Viewed' checkboxes are a documented independent collapse mechanism (docs 'Filtering files in a pull request') and can be a fallback.

Caveat from the 2015 Linguist thread: git attribute data 'isn't available to GitHub's front-end servers' when diffs are rendered; that was about vendored/ per-repo diff config and predates current generated handling, but it signals that the attribute is read from the repo state GitHub resolves for the diff (likely the head/merge commit), so the .gitattributes change must be in the same PR or already on the base branch. Which ref's .gitattributes governs a deletion-only file is unknown and is the central risk for a PR that deletes ~109 docs.

Existing repo rules: root .gitattributes (read, CRLF-terminated lines) only has '*.ps1 text eol=crlf', pinned reference-stub text/eol=crlf paths and '/reference-stubs/Siemens.Engineering.PublicKey.snk binary'. No linguist-* attributes exist anywhere. Five nested .gitattributes (tracked, 8 bytes '* -text' + LF) sit in docs/superpowers/acceptance/reports/inputs/{2026-10-29-hmi-write-timing-before,2026-10-30-hmi-write-native-rejections-live-cases, -local-session, -ui-compiles, 2026-10-30-hmi-write-timing-after}/. Verified with check-attr: a root linguist-generated rule and the nested 'text' unset combine because they are different attributes; precedence only matters per attribute (deeper file wins). No text/eol/binary conflicts. Adding linguist-generated does not change checkout bytes, so the byte-hash-sensitive tooling is unaffected. The .gz files currently have no rule; they are binary by content detection and the nested '* -text' already prevents eol conversion, so adding 'binary' is unnecessary and would change nothing relevant (binary = -diff -merge -text).

Interaction/gotchas: (1) The nested '* -text' files are themselves tracked files under inputs/ and will be matched by an inputs/** rule; if the evidence dirs are deleted the nested .gitattributes go with them, which is fine. (2) Do not put the new rules in a new nested docs/superpowers/.gitattributes unless wanted; a root block is easier to audit and uses root-anchored paths. (3) Do not use 'binary' or '-diff' to collapse; -diff only affects local git, not the web UI. (4) Live reports (docs/superpowers/acceptance/reports/*.md) must NOT be matched, or they would be collapsed in future PRs; they sit directly in reports/, so only the inputs/ subtree is matched. (5) Marking kept specs/plans: add '-linguist-generated' lines for the ~2 plans and ~2 specs after the broad rules.

contentBoundaryRules: Rule of one home. Each fact has one home; every other place links to it. ARCHITECTURE.md = how the system works now (present tense, kept current per its section 11). ADR = why, what was rejected, and what the choice still forces. IMPROVEMENT_LOG.md = open follow-ups, plus the latest completed entry. Reports = what was verified, on which candidate, the verdict, and the limits. SupportedOperations/ = the contract for each tool. AGENTS.md = current rules for agents and a history pointer.

An ADR states no current behavior details, field lists, schemas, limits or thresholds. It links to the ARCHITECTURE section or operation reference through `Current home`. If a sentence would need editing whenever the code changes, it belongs in ARCHITECTURE.md, not in an ADR.
An ADR carries no open work. It never lists follow-ups or TODOs; it links to the IMPROVEMENT_LOG heading. Items an ADR calls 'unresolved' are copied to the log if missing, not duplicated in the ADR.

An ADR carries no evidence: no test counts, coverage figures, timings, case matrices, candidate hashes or live-run narrative. It links to the report. It may state a verdict in a few words only (for example 'live-accepted in all three modes').
An ADR carries no execution steps: no task lists, PR sequences, worktree orchestration or wave plans. If the 'how' matters for the decision, it is one sentence under Decision.

An ADR is immutable once Accepted except for the Status and Superseded-by lines and link fixes. A reversal is a new ADR that supersedes the old one, so that the evolution stays visible. ARCHITECTURE.md is rewritten freely.

Admission test for a new ADR: a decision with a considered alternative or lasting constraint that a future maintainer could plausibly reverse by mistake (for example retiring tokens, bound-project-only content tools). Bug fixes, refactors, and feature additions with no alternative do not get an ADR; they go to the PR description and the reference doc.

Roadmap files (docs/roadmap/*, ROADMAP.md) hold intended future work only; completed phases are summarised by an ADR link, not by status narrative. AGENTS.md holds no dated 'live verified on ...' history; those sentences move into the matching ADR or report, and AGENTS.md keeps the current rule plus one pointer paragraph: history is in docs/adr/README.md and docs/superpowers/README.md; removed plans, specs and evidence are at tag docs-archive-2026-10-30.
